products.name: AssemblyAI
products.note: Speech AI API; transcription; summarization; PII redaction; enterprise security

reading.body:
AssemblyAI processes 2 million hours of audio daily through a speech-to-text API platform, meaning the infrastructure demands of voice AI are already substantial and growing.

Speech recognition sits between users and AI systems. Every transcribed conversation, meeting, or medical note is compute translated into text that downstream LLMs then process. AssemblyAI's scale suggests voice is not a niche interface but a primary input layer for enterprise AI workflows. The company's emphasis on real-time processing, low latency, and multiple concurrent APIs indicates that voice AI requires consistent, always-on infrastructure rather than batch processing. This creates steady demand for compute resources and the power and cooling systems that support them.

The data does not reveal AssemblyAI's infrastructure location, ownership model, or the actual compute hardware it runs on. It does not show growth rate, customer concentration, or whether processing happens on company-owned or rented infrastructure. The profile confirms the company exists and operates at scale, but gives no measure of power consumption, data center footprint, or grid impact. Understanding voice AI's role in grid constraints requires visibility into the physical buildout behind that 2 million hour daily figure.

profile_text.body:
AssemblyAI describes itself as a provider of AI models to transcribe and understand speech. Its site presents Speech AI models that convert speech to text and extract insights from voice data, and it lists a platform of APIs covering pre-recorded, realtime, and sync speech-to-text, speech understanding, voice agents, and dictation, along with Guardrails, an LLM Gateway, and a Playground for trying the models. The company also lists solutions for enterprises, startups, conversation intelligence, medical transcription, contact centers, voice agents, and AI notetakers, and says it offers an Applied AI team that works alongside customers.

The site states that AssemblyAI processes 2 million hours of audio every day and offers global redundancy and enterprise-grade uptime. It quotes a claim that the Universal-3.5 Pro speech model is best so far in terms of accuracy, latency, and language switching, and it describes routing between every LLM from one endpoint with built-in fallback so that models can be swapped and outages survived without changing code. The company positions the offering as Voice AI infrastructure that products can depend on at any scale, and says customers can choose which parts of the Voice AI stack they need.

AssemblyAI is tracked as a Voice and Audio product, described as a speech AI API with transcription, summarization, PII redaction, and enterprise security. No litigation or MCP server records are associated with it.
